base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user coordinate food for a community gathering by tracking attendees, their dietary needs, and any changes to the guest list or restrictions. When asked to evaluate specific dishes, check each one against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm organizing a potluck-style gathering for our neighborhood community group this Saturday. Can you help me figure out the food situation?

Mrs. Kowalski has been on a strict low-sodium diet since her heart episode in January, doctor's orders

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a neighborhood potluck gathering. You will introduce 5 households with various dietary needs, then update the guest list: Mrs. Kowalski's sodium restriction gets lifted by her doctor, the Nguyens join late with a shellfish allergy, and the Chens drop out but want a saved plate. At the end you will present a list of dishes and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at which dishes are problematic or tell the assistant what to check for.

You are a calm, friendly neighborhood organizer. You relay information about your neighbors in third person ('Mrs. Kowalski told me...', 'The Ahmeds are...'). You never express frustration or impatience. You treat guest list changes as perfectly normal.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

ground_truth.answer: Three dishes have issues: (1) Shrimp pad thai — shrimp is shellfish, Bao Nguyen has a severe shellfish allergy. (2) Caesar salad with croutons — croutons are made from bread (wheat/gluten), Tom Peterson is celiac and cannot eat gluten. (3) Peanut butter brownies — fine for the table since the Chens aren't attending, but MUST NOT be included on the Chens' saved plate because Mei has a severe peanut allergy. Lamb kofta with tahini sauce is fine — lamb is halal-compatible for the Ahmeds, no problematic allergens. Marinated chicken skewers with soy glaze are fine — chicken is halal-compatible, soy is not a listed allergen for anyone. Fruit salad is fine for everyone. Mrs. Kowalski's sodium restriction no longer applies — her doctor cleared her.

Caesar salad with croutons is problematic: croutons contain gluten (wheat), Tom Peterson is celiac and cannot eat gluten
Peanut butter brownies must not be included on the Chens' saved plate because Mei has a peanut allergy
Lamb kofta with tahini sauce is fine for everyone currently attending — agent confirms it is acceptable
Chicken skewers with soy glaze are fine for everyone currently attending — agent confirms they are acceptable
Fruit salad is fine for everyone — agent confirms it is acceptable
forbidden_elements: Flagging sodium content as a problem for Mrs. Kowalski (her restriction was lifted by her doctor)
Flagging lamb kofta as non-halal or problematic for the Ahmeds (lamb is halal-compatible)
Flagging chicken skewers as non-halal or problematic for the Ahmeds (chicken is halal-compatible)
Completely rejecting peanut butter brownies for the whole gathering (only problematic for the Chens' saved plate, fine for the table since Chens are not attending)
Saying Bao has a general seafood allergy (he specifically has shellfish allergy — fish would be fine)
Flagging any dish for the Chens as if they are attending in person (they are not present, only getting a saved plate)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint state management across a community meal planning conversation. Key tracking challenges: (1) The Ahmeds are Jordanian and devout → Muslim → halal (inferential chain) — but lamb and chicken are halal-compatible, so kofta and chicken skewers are FINE. This is an over-generalization trap: agents may incorrectly flag all meat as problematic for the Ahmeds. (2) Mrs. Kowalski's low-sodium restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation (doctor cleared her) — agents must not flag sodium as an issue. (3) The Nguyens join LATE with Bao's shellfish allergy — agents often forget late-joining entities. (4) The Chens EXIT but want a saved plate — Mei's peanut allergy applies ONLY to the saved plate, not to the shared table. (5) Tom Peterson's celiac diagnosis requires recognizing that croutons = bread = wheat = gluten. The probe includes 6 items: 2 clearly problematic (shrimp pad thai, Caesar salad), 1 scope-dependent (peanut butter brownies — fine for table, not for saved plate), 1 trap (lamb kofta — looks like it might violate halal but doesn't), 1 secondary trap (chicken skewers — same halal trap), and 1 clearly fine (fruit salad).

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
